sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (federal Common Law tradition coexisting with Quebec Civil Law for provincial corporate and commercial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) (provisional application 2017)
Canada-Netherlands Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1994)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, as amended (QBCA); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended (Part 21 beneficial ownership transparency); Quebec Regulation respecting the registre des entreprises, CQLR c S-31.1, r 1; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and its Regulations; FINTRAC Implementation Toolkit for reporting entities; Canada's Single Business Registry and Corporate Transparency Act initiatives; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, sections 462.31 (laundering proceeds of crime), 83.1-83.33 (terrorist financing offences); Revenu Québec registration and reporting obligations under the Tax Administration Act, CQLR c A-6.002.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence or Certificate of Status for every corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in jurisdiction of origin, e.g., Corporations Canada, Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, or Delaware Division of Corporations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is a Contracting Party to the Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents, effective January 11, 2024) or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Corporate Resolution/Power of Attorney for UBO disclosure sign-off and authorized representative appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate counsel or registered agent in the jurisdiction of incorporation, endorsed by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for the underling notarized instrument, followed by recognition by the Quebec competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Piercing Certificate and Affidavit (Quebec Form for Beneficial Ownership Declaration, including 25% threshold analysis and exceptions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Québec through the Registre de l'entreprise du Québec (REQ) digital portal, or a Quebec notary in the case of authentic deed filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notarial authentication only; no apostille required where the document originates in Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of valid passport or national identity document for each individual UBO and senior company officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, consular office, or apostille-issuing authority in the individual's country of nationality/residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the identity document country is a Convention member; otherwise full consular legalization chain (notarization -> foreign affairs -> consular certification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening against: FINTRAC policy on politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEPs); Global Affairs Canada listings under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the United Nations Act; UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for all US-dollar escrow rails and correspondent banking; Canadian domestic criminal-lifestyle records; and Interpol-issued notices. A documented negative screening result for every UBO, director, officer, and signatory is required within 30 days prior to incorporation filing, with a mandatory refresh at closing. Sector-level enhanced due diligence applies to aviation spares trading because of the medium-risk AML/CFT banking classification and cross-border escrow payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de l'entreprise du Québec (REQ) online name clearance portal, accessible via https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; combined with the federal Corporations Canada Nuans name search portal for Canadian business names at https://www.ic.gc.ca/consultation/NCR/BusinessNameResearch/index.html; and the federal NUANS-worthiness process for proposed corporative and business names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Quebec Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), sections 55 to 60, the corporate name must be exclusively in French unless it is a recognized trade-mark plus its French non-trademark form; the French form must be the predominant and established name. An English-only or non-French version may not be registered unless the name is accompanied by a French version in all official filings, signage, and correspondence, and the name complies with the regulation respecting the language of commerce and business. For transliteration, the name must be Latin-script compatible; any Cyrillic, CJK, or other script must be lawfully transliterated by a certified translator and submitted with a declaration of conformity to the 'francisation' doctrine.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ rejection, the incorporator must file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days, setting out the legal basis for name admissibility, including any Registre de l'entreprise du Québec prior-name conflict analysis, French-language compliance evidence, and the strategic commercial reasons for the preferred name. Should reconsideration fail, the applicant may file for judicial review before the Quebec Superior Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, Book VII, within 30 days of the adverse reconsideration decision. At the federal level, if the proposed name is only a provincial rejection, the entity may proceed as a Quebec business corporation without federal license; otherwise, for a federal incorporation, a new NUANS report is required. A one-time extension of the reservation may be available upon payment of the applicable REQ fee before the original 30-day window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is not permissible as the sole registered office for a Quebec business corporation because section 8(4) of the QBCA requires the registered office to be a physical address within Quebec that is maintained during ordinary business hours and capable of receiving legal process, notices, and official correspondence. For the distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus under ISIC 4659, Revenu Québec and the Canadian Financial Administration Act may additionally require a permanent commercial establishment, billing location, and a local agent for GST/QST and customs matters; a registered agent's commercial office is allowed only if it is a physical location with personnel, postal handling, and process service capacity, whereas a simple mail-forwarding address is rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% quantified risk: Revenu Québec typically visits commercial premises during retail or distribution GST/QST audits, and an aviation-parts trader dealing in surpluses and escrow payments is perceived as enhanced risk; therefore an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of registration has a high likelihood, and the occupant must maintain proper inventory records, title documentation, airworthiness traceability records, and UBO authority files for immediate production.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec business incorporation filing fee with registered office and UBO register declaration (REQ)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting fees payable to the registraire des entreprises du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: The statutory tariff is updated annually; preparation fees excluded.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and reservation (Quebec and federal combined)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed federal fee under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: Includes same-day online search and Quebec duplicate search.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address and process service (minimum first annual cycle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent corporate agent or law firm registered office service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Quebec market rate for physical registered office and process service, not a statutory tariff
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: Negotiable at CAD $150-250/month plus translation fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and consular legalization of the UBO piercing bundle (4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary and Global Affairs Canada authentication services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff prescribed by Quebec law; Global Affairs Canada consular authentication fee is CAD 45 per authentication, with additional consular fees for non-Hague countries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/sanctions screening and enhanced due diligence (OFAC, UN, OSFI, GAC and FINTRAC-parameter reports)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Automated AML data provider or in-house compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for medium-risk enhanced screening reports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: Requires monthly updating and evidence-retention per FINTRAC rules.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French-language legal review, translation and certification for corporate name and charter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-word/page translation tariff and juridic certification fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: Must include official statement of conformity to the Charter of the French Language.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business Corporation organizational acts drafting - articles of incorporation, minute book, share register, UBO chapters and banking authorization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Non-statutory market benchmark for a cross-border aviation-parts trading corporation; equivalent to CAD $1,200 - $1,800 + taxes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis_note: Fee varies with complexity and transaction timetable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, including sections 3 to 5 on constitution and articles, section 17 on issuance of the certificate of constitution, and applicable provisions on directors, officers, registers, and financial statements; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, on registration and enterprise information.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec), together with the required enterprise registration declaration and registered-office information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration permitted by the Business Corporations Act. The corporation should document subscription, consideration, and issuance in its securities register and board records. Quebec does not generally require incorporation capital to be deposited into a government escrow account; a commercial bank account may be opened after incorporation and funded under the board-approved subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept and record the subscription for the issued shares described in the incorporation documents, subject to receipt of the agreed consideration; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the Quebec address stated in the articles and enterprise-register filings; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until replacement or resignation; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the officers are authorized to complete enterprise-register, tax, banking, insurance, aviation-compliance, and licensing registrations and to execute all documents necessary to commence the Corporation’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Name and Incorporation Route
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a numbered Quebec corporation or conduct a French and English name search before filing. Confirm that the proposed name is not confusingly similar, misleading, or contrary to Quebec naming rules. If a federal corporation is selected instead, file under the Canada Business Corporations Act with Corporations Canada and register extra-provincially in Quebec.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company selection
Name-search results or name reservation evidence, if applicable
Director names, addresses, and consent information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace or amend the proposed name, provide clarifying evidence, or convert to a numbered corporation. Refile within the portal and pay any applicable amendment or priority-processing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation and Enterprise Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online incorporation and enterprise-registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the articles, registered-office details, director information, share provisions, French-language corporate information, and enterprise-registration declaration. Upload signed consents and supporting documents where requested. Use certified translations where documents are not in French or English. Pay the prescribed fee electronically and retain the confirmation number.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registry query within the stated deadline, correct defective articles or enterprise information, replace unacceptable corporate names, and resubmit the complete application. Preserve the original filing date where the registry permits corrective resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate and Complete Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and the Corporation’s registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate of constitution and enterprise-register extract. Open the corporate minute book, insert the articles and certificate, adopt the first board resolution, issue shares against documented consideration, record directors and officers, approve banking authorities, and maintain the securities register and beneficial-ownership records.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or uncertificated share records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct missing organizational records by subsequent board resolution, issue replacement certificates where necessary, amend registry information, and document all corrective actions in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Payroll, Import, and Controlled-Goods Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, Canada Border Services Agency, and Public Services and Procurement Canada Controlled Goods Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a business number, corporate income-tax account, GST/HST account, and Quebec QST account where thresholds or activities require registration. Register payroll accounts if employees are hired. Obtain an import-export RM account. Determine whether aircraft parts, technical data, or defense-related items are controlled goods or subject to export controls, and register or obtain permits before possession, transfer, or export where required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and enterprise-register extract
Export classification and permit files, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account information, provide additional identity or business-purpose evidence, and request review by the relevant agency. Do not import, possess, transfer, or export controlled items until the applicable registration or permit is effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Transport Canada Civil Aviation; Canada Border Services Agency; Global Affairs Canada; and applicable foreign aviation authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Define whether the business only trades parts or also performs inspection, repair, overhaul, testing, certification, or installation. For trading, maintain traceability, source documentation, serviceable or unserviceable status, airworthiness records, storage controls, and counterfeit-part procedures. If maintenance or release-to-service activity is performed, obtain the applicable Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization approval before operating. Obtain foreign approvals or export documentation where the transaction requires them.
required_dossiers: Certificates of conformity or airworthiness documentation
Transport Canada AMO application, if maintenance is performed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspend affected transactions, quarantine undocumented parts, correct records, notify customers or authorities where required, and submit an amended or supplementary approval application. Trading must not be represented as maintenance, certification, or release-to-service activity without the relevant approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Municipal Occupancy, Fire, and Warehouse Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Quebec municipality, municipal fire safety service, building authority, and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning and permitted warehouse use before signing the lease. Obtain occupancy or change-of-use approval where required. Complete fire prevention review, emergency exits, fire-protection equipment, hazardous-material storage review, structural-load confirmation, and workplace health-and-safety measures. Ensure storage racks and floor loads are suitable for aircraft components and batteries, if any.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies identified in the inspection, obtain revised drawings or engineering certification, restrict occupancy to approved areas, and request reinspection before commencing the affected operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Civil Aviation for aviation maintenance approvals; Public Services and Procurement Canada Controlled Goods Directorate for controlled goods; Global Affairs Canada for export permits; and the relevant Quebec municipality for zoning and occupancy. Ordinary wholesale trading of civil aircraft parts does not, by itself, require a general Quebec manufacturing licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization Certificate under the Canadian Aviation Regulations, Part V, Subpart 71, if the business performs maintenance, repair, overhaul, inspection, testing, or release-to-service functions. A pure distributor generally operates without an aviation maintenance certificate but must comply with applicable import, export, controlled-goods, sanctions, and product-traceability requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinary aircraft-parts warehousing and distribution is generally exempt from a project-level EIA. Environmental authorization under section 22 of the Quebec Environment Quality Act may be required for activities involving hazardous substances, waste storage or treatment, significant wastewater discharge, soil disturbance, emissions, fuel systems, or other activities likely to affect the environment. A project-specific assessment may apply to prescribed high-impact projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Quebec Environment Quality Act and applicable regulations, municipal sewer bylaws, federal Fisheries Act section 36 restrictions on deleterious deposits, hazardous-waste handling rules, spill-prevention requirements, and applicable VOC and air-emission limits. Maintain manifests and authorized disposal records for oils, solvents, batteries, contaminated materials, and other regulated waste. No industrial discharge or regulated emission should begin without the required authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal occupancy and fire-safety approval, maintain compliant exits, alarms, extinguishers, emergency lighting, evacuation procedures, and hazardous-material controls, and complete structural-load and racking inspections for the warehouse. Comply with Quebec occupational health and safety requirements administered by CNESST, including worker training, personal protective equipment, lifting controls, battery and chemical storage, incident reporting, and workplace inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the CRA Business Registration Online portal for obtaining a Business Number and program accounts; Revenu Quebec administers Quebec Sales Tax (QST) registration and compliance through its online services portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a nine-digit CRA Business Number (BN) and register the applicable CRA program accounts, including GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import-export (RM), as relevant. A non-resident corporation may apply through CRA Business Registration Online where eligible, by telephone, or through the prescribed non-resident registration process, providing legal name, incorporation details, registered address, directors, business activities, expected Canadian taxable supplies, and authorized representative information. A corporation making taxable supplies in Quebec must separately register for QST with Revenu Quebec unless a specific exemption applies. The entity must maintain Canadian books and records, file required GST/HST and QST returns, collect tax at the applicable rate, and update registration information promptly. Importers must obtain and use an RM import-export program account through the Canada Border Services Agency and CRA systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally separate taxable persons and have no United States-style federal check-the-box election. Available elections are transaction- or status-specific, including corporate reorganizations under the Income Tax Act, amalgamations, wind-ups, section 216 elections for certain Canadian rental income of non-residents, and elections affecting GST/HST treatment such as the closely related election and joint venture elections where statutory conditions are met. Quebec corporate tax treatment generally follows the federal corporate form but requires separate Quebec filings and elections where applicable. Partnership and trust classifications are determined under Canadian law and are not freely elected by a corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.corporate_income_tax_identity: A corporation resident in Canada is generally subject to federal corporate income tax on worldwide income and Quebec corporate income tax on income allocated to Quebec. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada may be subject to Canadian tax on Canadian-source business income and may have branch tax exposure. Corporate residence depends principally on incorporation and central management and control principles, subject to treaty rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), together with Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Quebec generally applies GST at the federal level and QST at the provincial level rather than HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, including supplies of associated persons, measured under the small-supplier rules generally by reference to a single calendar quarter or the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. The threshold applies to GST/HST registration; Quebec QST registration generally follows separate Quebec rules and may be required for persons carrying on business in Quebec or making taxable supplies there, subject to limited small-supplier and non-resident rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.economic_nexus_and_registration_rules: A person making taxable supplies in Canada in the course of commercial activity must register for GST/HST when the applicable small-supplier threshold is exceeded or when voluntary registration is elected. A non-resident may be required to register where it makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not relieved by the small-supplier rules or a special non-resident regime. Registration may be required before importing commercial goods, depending on the structure and importer-of-record arrangements. QST registration is generally required for persons carrying on commercial activities in Quebec and making taxable supplies in Quebec, including certain non-resident suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not generally impose a universal real-time electronic invoicing clearance mandate for ordinary business-to-business supplies. GST/HST and QST invoices must contain prescribed information, including supplier identity and registration numbers, date, consideration, tax rate, and tax amount where applicable. Electronic invoices are permitted if integrity, authenticity, accessibility, and record-retention requirements are satisfied. CRA and Revenu Quebec generally support electronic filing and payment, but ordinary invoices are not required to receive prior government clearance or a digital fiscal stamp. Customs filings and import/export data may be submitted electronically through CBSA systems, including the CARM system for commercial imports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.aviation_parts_specific_indirect_tax_not: Sales of aircraft parts are ordinarily taxable unless a specific zero-rating or exemption applies. Classification as aircraft equipment or parts does not by itself make a supply zero-rated. Import GST and, where applicable, QST may arise at importation, subject to customs valuation, importer-of-record status, relief provisions, and recoverability through input tax credits or Quebec input tax refunds. Export controls, controlled-goods rules, customs tariff classification, and aviation regulatory approvals are separate from GST/HST and QST treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Commercial goods supplied for export from Canada may generally be zero-rated for GST/HST where the supplier ships or delivers the goods outside Canada, the recipient exports the goods under qualifying statutory conditions, or another prescribed export rule applies. The supplier must retain sufficient evidence that the goods were exported and must satisfy the applicable timing and delivery conditions. A supplier generally cannot treat goods as zero-rated merely because the purchaser is non-resident or intends to export them later. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where the specific export-of-services rules apply; exclusions can cover services connected with real property, tangible personal property, or services performed in Canada. QST zero-rating or export treatment must be tested separately under Quebec legislation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the goods, buyer, seller, value, currency, and delivery terms
Export declaration or applicable Canada Border Services Agency export filing, including Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) data where required
Customs release and import entry or equivalent destination-country import evidence where available
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, freight-forwarder record, or other carrier documentation showing shipment outside Canada
Packing list and serial-number or part-number records for aircraft parts
Proof of delivery or receipt outside Canada
Purchase order, sales contract, and payment records
GST/HST and QST invoices showing the applicable zero-rated treatment and registration numbers
Inward remittance evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation; Canada does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a condition of export zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.fx_repatriation_rule: Canada has no general foreign-exchange control regime requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days or another fixed statutory period. Proceeds may generally be retained offshore, subject to Canadian income-tax, transfer-pricing, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, customs, and financial-reporting requirements. Contractual financing, banking, export-credit, or regulatory arrangements may impose separate deadlines.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.refund_and_input_tax_recovery: A GST/HST registrant may generally claim input tax credits for GST/HST incurred on commercial inputs to the extent acquired, imported, or brought into a participating province for consumption, use, or supply in commercial activities. A QST registrant may generally claim input tax refunds for eligible QST incurred in commercial activities. Documentation must identify the supplier, registration number where required, date, consideration, tax amount, and nature of the supply. Net tax or QST refund claims are subject to statutory filing periods, documentary support, and audit verification.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA or Revenu Quebec may reassess tax not collected, deny input tax credits or input tax refunds, impose interest, and assess penalties where export evidence is incomplete, inaccurate, or fraudulent. A person that knowingly or recklessly participates in false invoicing, fictitious exports, false customs declarations, or fraudulent refund claims may face gross-negligence penalties, civil fraud penalties, prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under applicable federal or Quebec law. Amounts improperly refunded or credited may be recovered retrospectively with interest and penalties. Customs violations may additionally result in seizure, monetary penalties, accounting-document demands, AMPS penalties, import-export account consequences, or prosecution. Documentary records should generally be retained for at least six years after the end of the relevant tax year, subject to longer periods where an audit, objection, appeal, reassessment, or statutory exception applies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no separate general foreign-exchange administration imposing routine capital controls; financial institutions and payment providers remain subject to the Bank Act, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, sanctions legislation, and applicable Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada does not generally require foreign-exchange licensing, mandatory repatriation, capital-account registration, or approval for foreign ownership, shareholder loans, dividends, or intercompany transfers. Profit remittances are subject to corporate income tax compliance, withholding tax rules under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, applicable Canada tax treaties, transfer-pricing documentation, thin-capitalization limits, shareholder-benefit rules, solvency requirements, sanctions screening, and bank source-of-funds controls. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, controlled goods, or unusual aviation counterparties may be blocked or escalated. Quebec entities must also maintain appropriate corporate, tax, customs, and commercial records and may require French-language documentation or communications under Quebec language rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no general statutory deadline, mandatory conversion ratio, or compulsory surrender requirement for export proceeds. The corporation may retain export receipts in Canadian dollars or foreign currency, subject to contractual, tax, accounting, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Export documentation must support customs treatment, origin, valuation, end use, and any zero-rated GST/HST treatment. Foreign-currency receipts should be recorded using an appropriate Canadian accounting and tax methodology, with realized and unrealized foreign-exchange gains or losses documented. Proceeds from controlled aviation articles remain subject to applicable export-control, sanctions, customs, and end-use requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection, foreign-currency accounts, and operational transfers; low as a substitute for a Canadian deposit-taking bank or aviation-trade bank. An offshore electronic-money institution may provide services only within its licensed permissions and must satisfy Canadian payment, AML, sanctions, consumer-protection, data, and foreign-exchange requirements applicable to its activities. It cannot be assumed to provide Canadian deposit insurance, Canadian-dollar clearing, documentary trade finance, escrow services, or unrestricted access to Canadian domestic payment rails. Canadian-resident payment activities may trigger registration or licensing under the Retail Payment Activities Act and related requirements, while money services businesses may require FINTRAC registration. Banks may decline fintech-originated funds where beneficial ownership, source of wealth, licensing, or transaction purpose is unclear.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by directors is not generally required by Canadian statute for corporate account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted by the selected bank after verification of the corporation, directors, beneficial owners, signing officers, business address, tax residency, source of funds, expected transaction profile, and aviation-trade activities. A bank may require video interviews, notarized or certified documents, branch attendance, Canadian-resident signing authority, or enhanced review for non-resident owners, complex ownership, foreign funding, high-value aircraft parts, sanctions exposure, or unusual jurisdictions. The corporation should obtain a Quebec or federal corporate profile, business number, organizational documents, registers, and evidence of an operating Canadian business address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or layered ownership involving nominee shareholders, trusts, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to identify every individual beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles and corporate profile; shareholder register; ownership chart to natural persons; beneficial-owner declarations; passports and residential-address evidence; trust deeds and trustee documentation where relevant; director and officer register; board resolution; and written explanation of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection with unexplained source of funds or transfers through unrelated third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns; sale-of-business or investment documentation; lender commitment; source-of-wealth narrative; originating-bank details; SWIFT payment evidence; and confirmation that the remitter is the shareholder, lender, or documented financing intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation-parts trading involving sanctioned countries, military end users, restricted aircraft, dual-use articles, or unusual transshipment routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product catalogue and part numbers; manufacturer and traceability records; certificates of conformity or airworthiness documentation where applicable; end-user and end-use certificates; customer and supplier screening; export and import classification; permits or written non-permit determinations; sanctions screening logs; shipping route; freight and customs documents; and internal escalation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid incoming and outgoing wires inconsistent with the stated surplus-aircraft-parts business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; expected countries, currencies, counterparties, and monthly transaction volumes; purchase orders; sales contracts; invoices; shipping documents; customs entries; inventory records; gross-margin analysis; treasury policy; and reconciliation demonstrating the commercial purpose of each material payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, politically exposed persons, or intermediaries with no apparent commercial function.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty ownership and screening reports; adverse-media review; PEP assessment; sanctions-screening results; intermediary agreement; commission rationale; beneficial-purpose statement; enhanced due-diligence approval; payment-chain diagram; and senior management authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among corporate name, Quebec registration, tax number, website, business address, invoices, or account signatories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extract; CRA business-number confirmation; Quebec enterprise registration where applicable; lease or utility evidence; website and branded-domain ownership; organizational chart; specimen invoices; board resolutions; signing mandate; and written explanation for any trade name, registered office, or jurisdictional difference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash-intensive settlement, cryptocurrency, or payment platforms unrelated to the corporate treasury structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal and cash settlement; corporate payment policy; bank reconciliation procedure; approved-account list; accounting controls; vendor onboarding standards; explanation of any historical exception; and remediation evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscribed share capital and shareholder loans from the named investor or documented lender directly to the corporation's Canadian bank account through SWIFT or the bank's approved correspondent channel. Use the corporation's exact legal name, Canadian account number, transit and institution numbers, SWIFT/BIC, currency, and registered address. Canada generally has no statutory foreign-capital purpose-code regime; the bank should nevertheless receive a clear payment narrative such as 'share capital subscription' or 'shareholder loan under agreement [reference]'. Before release, provide the subscription or loan agreement, board approval, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, lender identity, ownership percentage, tax treatment, and expected use of funds. Record the transaction in the general ledger and corporate registers, reconcile the incoming wire, and assess withholding tax, transfer pricing, thin capitalization, interest deductibility, and related-party reporting. Do not route funds through unrelated third-party accounts or split transfers to avoid review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian bank accounts for supplier payments and maintain a transaction-level audit trail. SWIFT MT103 or its current ISO 20022 equivalent is appropriate for direct commercial wires; include the exact beneficiary, bank identifiers, invoice number, purchase-order number, part numbers, shipment reference, currency, and truthful payment purpose. For high-value or new-counterparty purchases, use a documentary commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, escrow, or controlled disbursement arrangement negotiated with the bank. A commercial LC should specify compliant presentation documents, including commercial invoice, packing list, air waybill or bill of lading, customs information, insurance evidence where applicable, certificates of conformity or traceability, and end-user or export-control documentation when relevant. Screen all parties, aircraft, parts, routes, banks, freight forwarders, and end users against Canadian sanctions and export-control requirements before payment, shipment, and document release. Retain invoices, contracts, customs records, payment messages, screening evidence, and reconciliations for the applicable statutory and bank retention periods.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD or CAD/EUR forward contracts with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, supported by documented underlying exposures, approved treasury limits, counterparty credit review, confirmations, valuation, and settlement controls.

Currency options, including purchased vanilla options and approved collars, where the corporation understands premium, exercise, accounting, suitability, and documentation requirements and does not create unapproved speculative exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to dealer eligibility, local-law analysis, sanctions screening, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, reporting, and confirmation that the transaction hedges a genuine commercial exposure.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA documentation, counterparty credit support, valuation, collateral, accounting, derivatives reporting, and board-approved risk limits.
Foreign-currency bank balances and natural hedges between receipts and payments in the same currency, with segregation of operating liquidity, minimum cash thresholds, and documented authorization.

Hedging is not a substitute for export-control or sanctions compliance. Speculative derivatives, unapproved leverage, transactions with unlicensed dealers, and hedges lacking an identifiable commercial exposure should be prohibited under the treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) — corporate, director, registered-office and beneficial-owner data, filed via REQ online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's registration date with the REQ (anniversary-based cycle; reminder issued by REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 30 late-filing surcharge (≈ USD 22); no certificate of attestation issued while in default; after two consecutive years without a valid annual declaration the Registraire may strike the registration or administratively dissolve the corporation under the LPLE and QBCA; directors remain liable for post-dissolution activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) — applicable to corporations incorporated or continued under the Canada Business Corporations Act and extra-provincially registered in Québec; confirms status of directors and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada — Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation or continuance (CBCA s. 263(1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee is added for delayed filing; the Director may dissolve the corporation under CBCA s. 265 after two consecutive years of failure to file, following written notice (CBCA s. 264); revival requires an order plus payment of all fees and arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) — holding and minuting the shareholders' meeting, election of directors, presentation of financial statements, and appointment or unanimous waiver of auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None — records retained in the statutory minute book; director identity flow is reported to REQ and/or Corporations Canada through the annual declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; each subsequent AGM within 15 months of the preceding AGM (QBCA s. 168; CBCA s. 132(1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty; non-compliance exposes directors to shareholder oppression applications, requisition of meetings, court orders to convene the AGM, and inability to pass valid resolutions necessary for annual declarations and financing transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register Audit — annual review and reconciliation of the Register of Members, Register of Directors, share-transfer ledger, Minute Book and UBO register against the REQ/Corporations Canada records; presentation of audit findings to shareholders at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance process — no regulatory filing; the audit report is placed in the minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the annual declaration is filed (within 60 days after anniversary) and before the AGM; material control changes additionally require an updating declaration within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a filing obligation; unresolved register discrepancies block accurate annual declarations, delay financing and due-diligence, and constitute evidence of governance failure relevant to director liability under the QBCA/CBCA and AML enhanced-due-diligence reviews triggered by the aviation-spares distribution profile.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — CRA, including international transaction disclosure (T106/T1134 where applicable) and provincial allocations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month in arrears (maximum 12 months); repeat offenders (late-filing penalty assessed in any of the prior 3 years) incur 10% plus 2% per full month (maximum 20 months); interest accrues on unpaid balances; unreported-income penalties and separate information-return penalties apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17) — provincial corporate tax, minimum tax and installment reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end, aligned with the federal T2 filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due plus 1% per full month of arrears (maximum 12 months); repeat-filing penalties of 10% plus 2% per full month (maximum 20 months); interest at the prescribed rate; default assessments may be issued where the CO-17 is not filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Québec (QBCA) and the federal CBCA impose no revenue/asset threshold for audit. An independent auditor and audit are compulsory for distributing corporations (publicly held or listed securities). A non-distributing, closely held corporation may waive the audit and the auditor appointment each year by unanimous shareholders' resolution (QBCA ss. 203-206; CBCA s. 163), provided the corporation is not an issuer; lenders, OEM accreditation programs, insurers and CRA transfer-pricing procedures commonly impose an audit covenant notwithstanding the statutory waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board (AcSB) for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may elect either IFRS or ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook — Canadian private-enterprise GAAP). An aviation-parts distribution corporation with cross-border payments, US-counterparty contracts and lender oversight typically prepares IFRS-compliant financial statements, with ASPE available where all-arms-length domestic reporting suffices.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Québec (LPLE) requires every registered legal person to identify in its annual declaration all 'persons having control': natural persons holding at least 25% of the voting rights, at least 25% of the shares, or exercising de facto control. The annual declaration is filed within 60 days of the REQ registration anniversary and constitutes the annual UBO confirmation; a share transfer crossing the 25% threshold or any other material control change must be filed as an updating declaration within 30 days of the change and recorded in the company's internal register. Federal corporations must also maintain the CBCA register of individuals with significant control, align every transfer with the UBO ledger, and confirm accuracy annually when the federal annual return is certified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) maintained under QBCA/CBCA
Register of Share Transfers and Share Allotments
Minute Book (board and shareholder minutes, written resolutions, by-laws)
Register of Persons Having Control (UBO register) under the LPLE/CBCA significant-control regime
Registered Office records (attestation certificates, articles, and authorization records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 1,200 per year (CAD 475 – 1,600): typical Québec registered-office and corporate-secretary agent band; Montreal full-service agents charging USD 600 – 1,000 per year for preparation and filing of declarations, AGM administration and register maintenance.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 25,000 (CAD 11,000 – 34,000) for a full certified audit of an active aviation-parts distribution corporation (IFRS/ASPE); if the statutory audit is waived but a lender mandates a review engagement, the professional fee approximates USD 3,500 – 8,000 (CAD 5,000 – 11,000).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific incentive for wholesale trade; general federal investment tax credits (SR&ED) and accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) on Class 8 machinery/equipment may apply. Small business deduction (SBD) not available if non-resident owned or exceeds CAD 15M taxable capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA's e-file (corporation internet filing). Provincial: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return via Revenu Québec's CLICK electronic service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly tax instalments for federally and provincially resident corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 6 months after the fiscal year-end; tax payment due 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for some CCPCs with small business income). No extension for payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from wholesale distribution of aircraft parts, including proceeds from sale of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the corporation is a non-resident doing business in Canada, report only Canadian-source business income and ensure allocation of income in accordance with permanent establishment (PE) rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold (inventory acquisition), administrative expenses, interest, and other allowable deductions, including transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be traced to Canadian-source income and satisfy reasonableness and documentary requirements under s.67.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income after applicable deductions and loss carryforwards, subject to Part I tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute on the basis of the Canada–foreign country tax treaty relief for PE income allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate tax at 15% (after provincial tax abatement for certain provinces, not Quebec) plus any applicable additional taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are subject to Part I tax on Canadian business income and Part XIII withholding for dividends/royalties paid to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income from commercial activity; must reconcile to T2 federal income with Quebec-specific adjustments (e.g., Quebec capital allowance).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Quebec PE must report Quebec-source income and file CO-17.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after deducting federal vs. provincial adjustments and loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Quebec's double-weighting of sales apportionment for allocation of income to non-resident corporates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec provincial corporate tax at 11.5% computed on taxable income, subject to provincial abatements and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, only Quebec-source income within the PE is taxed; export sales from Canada attributed to Quebec may be taxable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% for each full month, up to 12 months; repeat failure 10% plus 2% per month. Quebec: similar penalty under the Taxation Act (s.17.3), 5% plus 1% monthly up to 12 months; provincial interest compounded daily.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to non-residents (domestic rate). Treaty relieving rates: 5% for a US corporation holding at least 10% voting shares; 15% for portfolio investors under Canada-US DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced rate, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by its home jurisdiction and provide it to the Canadian payer. The payer must retain the TRC and complete a residency declaration (CRA Form NR301 – Treaty-Based Withholding Waiver). Original TRC and copies of the DTA application must be kept in the corporation's books for CRA audit verification. Filing such forms is required at or before payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties – 25%; interest paid to arm's-length non-residents – 0% (Canada's domestic exemption for arm's-length interest); non-arm's-length interest – 25%. Canada-US treaty: royalties – 10% for industrial, commercial, or equipment use; 0% for certain copyright; interest – 15% generally, 0% for government owned or pension fund, 0% for arm's-length interest under treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions (Form T106 filing threshold). Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is statutorily required for all reportable transactions under s.247(4) and may be requested by the CRA; a CRA audit will expect full Local File and Master File alignment with OECD Guidelines if gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies the Economic Substance Doctrine through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245) and the doctrine of 'sham' under common law. For treaty benefits, an entity must demonstrate substantial business activities (real presence, active management, Canadian bank accounts, and payroll). The DTA may be denied if the structure lacks commercial substance. No standalone ESR regime, but the CRA may challenge shell arrangements with no business purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False or misleading income reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting revenues from surplus aircraft part sales, inflating expense deductions, or failing to report Canadian-source income of a non-resident PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act s.239: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment up to 5 years. Quebec Taxation Act s.36.1 mirrors federal criminal sanctions. Civil penalty under s.163(2) is mandatory: 25% of the amount of tax attempted to evade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under s.227.1 for unpaid corporate tax withholdings and for civil restitution if they participated in or acquiesced to the evasion. Travel bans (RCMP-facilitated) and asset freezes are possible in criminal proceedings; imprisonment is a direct liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating in Quebec without actual office, employees, or decision-making functions, while routing profits to low-tax jurisdictions via intercompany transactions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess and deny treaty benefits, apply GAAR on a tax benefit, and impose significant penalties. DTA relief can be voided resulting in full Canadian withholding tax liability. In Quebec, under the Business Corporations Act, the corporation may be involuntarily dissolved for patterns of non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for CRA assessments, including up to 100% of the tax shortfall if they signed false returns (s.163.2). Directors of sham corporations may be held personally for losses in civil suits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting high-volume SWIFT wire or escrow transactions without a compliant anti-money laundering (AML) program, particularly when dealing with sanctioned aviation counterparties or using cash/crypto rails for settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act fines up to CAD 2 million per administrative violation; FINTRAC penalties up to CAD 500,000. Criminal fines and confiscation of goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for failure to establish adequate AML controls; criminal convictions can lead to imprisonment (up to 5 years) and prohibition from acting as directors. Travel bans and extradition risks arise where payments are tied to international trade offenses.
